flood.name: Göbekli Tepe
flood.source: Dietrich et al. 2013, Antiquity — Enclosure D, radiocarbon dated ~9500-8500 BC; the site's function is actively debated (Schmidt 2006 'cult center built by hunter-gatherers' hypothesis vs. Clare et al. 2019 revised, more settlement-like interpretation)
flood.credit: Photograph: Erkcan, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The First Pottery
flood.source: Tokyo National Museum object label (Hinamiyama site, Yokohama, Kanagawa): Incipient Jōmon pottery, dated 11,000-7,000 BC — a wide range reflecting genuine, ongoing dispute over calibration of the earliest Jōmon phase; 10,000 years ago is a conservative point within that cited range
flood.credit: Photograph: User:PHG, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Tower of Jericho
flood.source: Kenyon, K. (1957) Digging Up Jericho; the PPNA stone tower at Tell es-Sultan is radiocarbon-dated to c. 8000 BC. Its purpose is genuinely disputed — see Bar-Yosef, O. (1986) 'The Walls of Jericho: An Alternative Interpretation,' Current Anthropology 27(2), which argues against the standard 'defensive wall' reading
flood.credit: Photograph: Reinhard Dietrich, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Çatalhöyük
flood.source: Mellaart, J. (1962) 'Excavations at Çatal Hüyük, 1961,' Anatolian Studies 12, pl. XIVb — wall painting of dancers in leopard skins, from a level Mellaart's original excavation chronology places in the 6th millennium BC
flood.credit: Photographer unknown; reproduced in B. Brentjes, 'Das Leopardenfell im Alten Orient,' Das Pelzgewerbe XVI (1965), after Mellaart 1962; Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Early Farming: The Flint Sickle
flood.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art, collection object record 547151 (metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/547151); excavated by the Vienna Academy of Science, 1929-30, at Merimda Beni Salama, Western Nile Delta, Egypt; catalogued 4500-4000 BC. Substituted for the candidate 'farming in the Fertile Crescent': this is Nile Valley Neolithic farming technology, geographically adjoining but not identical to the Levant/Mesopotamia core of the Fertile Crescent -- no equivalently-licensed Levantine/Mesopotamian sickle of this age was found
flood.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund; CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

flood.name: Copper Smelting
flood.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art, accession 38.40.396; excavated 1937 near Nishapur, northeastern Iran; catalogued to the 5th-3rd millennium BC (Chalcolithic-Early Bronze Age) -- a wide range for this specific find context, used here at its midpoint
flood.credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art; CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

flood.name: The Narmer Palette
flood.source: Egyptian Museum, Cairo (JE 32169); ceremonial siltstone palette from Hierakonpolis bearing King Narmer's name-glyphs, among the earliest attested Egyptian writing; Naqada III / Dynasty 0, c. 3100 BC (Egyptian Museum, Cairo collection record; excavated by J.E. Quibell, 1898)
flood.credit: Photographer unknown (PD-old-100, 2D reproduction of an ancient artefact)

flood.name: The Great Pyramid of Giza
flood.source: Pyramid of Khufu, Giza Plateau, Old Kingdom Fourth Dynasty; completed c. 2560 BC (Encyclopaedia Britannica; Mark Lehner, The Complete Pyramids, 1997). Photographed from a balloon, 21 November 1904.
flood.credit: Eduard Spelterini (1852-1931); scanned from Über den Wolken, Brunner & Co, Zürich 1928

flood.name: Stonehenge
flood.source: English Heritage: the standard excavation chronology (Cleal, Walker & Montague 1995, 'Stonehenge in its Landscape') dates erection of the sarsen circle and trilithons to approximately 2500 BC via radiocarbon dating
flood.credit: Photograph: uploader Hasso~commonswiki (credited per Commons copyright assumption), Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Cuneiform Tablet
flood.source: Small clay tablet recording an account of bricks carried by workers, Akkadian language, Early Old Babylonian period, c. 2000 BC (The Letterform Archive, object record lfa_antiquarianleaves_0010)
flood.credit: The Letterform Archive; translation assistance by Manuel Molina

flood.name: The Code of Hammurabi
flood.source: Louvre Museum, Sb 8; diorite stele of Hammurabi, king of Babylon, reign c. 1792-1750 BC (Louvre Museum collection record)
flood.credit: Rmashhadi, Wikimedia Commons (released into the public domain)

flood.name: Shang Dynasty Oracle Bone
flood.source: National Museum of China; ox bone from the Bīn diviner group, Period I, reign of King Wu Ding, Late Shang dynasty, c. 1200 BC (David N. Keightley, Sources of Shang History: The Oracle-Bone Inscriptions of Bronze-Age China, 1978)
flood.credit: Gary Todd

flood.name: Inscribed Bronze Zun Vessel
flood.source: National Palace Museum, Taipei; bronze zun wine vessel with cast inscription, Late Shang dynasty, 13th-11th century BC (National Palace Museum collection record)
flood.credit: Gary Todd

flood.name: Lydian Gold Stater
flood.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art, accession 26.59.2; gold stater struck under Croesus, king of Lydia, c. 560-546 BC (Metropolitan Museum of Art collection record)
flood.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access)

flood.name: The Parthenon
flood.source: Acropolis of Athens; Doric temple to Athena built 447-432 BC under Pericles, architects Iktinos and Kallikrates (Acropolis Museum, Athens; Acropolis Restoration Service YSMA)
flood.credit: Jebulon, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Terracotta Army
flood.source: Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang, Lintong, Xi'an; life-size terracotta soldier from the burial complex of China's First Emperor, interred c. 210 BC (UNESCO World Heritage listing 'Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor'; Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum)
flood.credit: Gary Lee Todd, Ph.D., Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Rosetta Stone
flood.source: British Museum EA24 — decree of Memphis, 196 BC; shown here as an engraved facsimile plate (not a photograph of the stone) published in 'Gallery of Antiquities, Selected from the British Museum', 1842
flood.credit: Unknown author

flood.name: Paper in Han China
flood.source: Fangmatan Tomb 5, Gansu; fragment of a hemp-fibre paper map found on the chest of the tomb occupant, tomb dated to the early Western Han, early 2nd century BC (Tsien Tsuen-Hsuin, Paper and Printing, in Needham (ed.), Science and Civilisation in China, vol. 5:1, 1985; 1986 excavation report)
flood.credit: Unknown photographer (PD-old, artefact photograph)

flood.name: The Great Stupa at Sanchi
flood.source: Stupa 1, Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh; Ashokan brick core c. 260 BC, enlarged with the stone dome casing, balustrade, and carved torana gateways (shown) added 2nd-1st century BC (Archaeological Survey of India; UNESCO World Heritage listing 'Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi')
flood.credit: RohitChohan25, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Colosseum
flood.source: Flavian Amphitheatre, Rome; built 70-80 AD under emperors Vespasian and Titus, dedicated 80 AD (Parco Archeologico del Colosseo; UNESCO World Heritage listing 'Historic Centre of Rome')
flood.credit: Wilfredor, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Nazca Lines
flood.source: Nazca monkey geoglyph, Peru; Nazca-culture ground drawing, most figures dated to roughly 100 BC - AD 300 on ceramic and stratigraphic evidence (UNESCO World Heritage listing 'Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa'; Silverman & Proulx, The Nasca, 2002). Exact date range for individual figures remains debated among specialists.
flood.credit: Maria Reiche, 1953 (dedicated to the public domain by the photographer)

flood.name: Maya Glyphs
flood.source: Maya stela fragment, Metropolitan Museum of Art (Michael C. Rockefeller Memorial Collection, acc. 1978.412.75b); the museum dates the carved glyph panel to the 4th-9th century AD. yearsAgo reflects the early (4th-century) end of that range; the object may in fact postdate this era's AD 500 boundary.
flood.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access)

flood.name: Hagia Sophia
flood.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hagia Sophia': built 532-537 CE in Constantinople under the Byzantine emperor Justinian I.
flood.credit: Detroit Publishing Co. photochrom print, c. 1897; Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Bayeux Tapestry (detail: Archbishop Stigand)
flood.source: Bayeux Museum; the embroidered wool-on-linen tapestry is generally dated to the 1070s, within a decade of the 1066 Battle of Hastings it depicts, likely completed for the 1077 dedication of Bayeux Cathedral.
flood.credit: Unknown embroiderers; photograph by Myrabella, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Sankore Mosque, Timbuktu
flood.source: BlackPast.org, 'Sankore Mosque and University (c. 1100- )'; sources disagree on the founding date, ranging from a legendary 988-989 CE foundation to a 14th-century expansion into a madrasa under Mali Empire patronage (UNESCO World Heritage listing for Timbuktu cites the 14th-15th centuries for the city's three great mosques). Dated here to the broad c. 1100 CE anchor point used by BlackPast.org.
flood.credit: Photograph by Edmond Fortier (1862-1928), 1905-1906; Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Angkor Wat
flood.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Angkor Wat': built in the 12th century (c. 1113-1150 CE) by the Khmer king Suryavarman II.
flood.credit: Photograph by Emile Gsell (1838-1879), 1866; Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Great Zimbabwe (Great Enclosure outer wall)
flood.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'Great Zimbabwe (11th-15th Century)'; UNESCO World Heritage listing (Great Zimbabwe National Monument): the site was built and expanded c. 1100-1450 CE; the Great Enclosure's dry-stone outer wall, pictured, belongs to the 13th-15th century building phase.
flood.credit: David Randall-MacIver, 1906 excavation photograph; Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Yuan-dynasty bronze hand-gun
flood.source: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution, Beijing: bronze hand-cannon bearing an inscription corresponding to 1351 CE (Zhizheng reign era, Yuan dynasty) — one of the earliest precisely-dated firearms, alongside the 1288 Heilongjiang and 1298 'Xanadu Gun' specimens described in Needham's Science and Civilisation in China.
flood.credit: Photograph by Gary Todd, Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: Machu Picchu
flood.source: Burger et al., 'New AMS dates for Machu Picchu: results and implications', Antiquity (2021, Yale-led radiocarbon study): construction/occupation began c. 1420 CE, roughly two decades earlier than the traditional c. 1440-1450 CE estimate. NOTE: this postdates the 500-1400 CE medieval window by design brief's own acknowledgment.
flood.credit: Photograph by Hiram Bingham III, 1912 (Yale Peruvian Expedition / National Geographic); Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Gutenberg Bible
flood.source: World Digital Library / Library of Congress — Gutenberg Bible, printed by Johann Gutenberg, Mainz, c. 1454-1456 (movable-type printing)
flood.credit: Johann Gutenberg (printer); digitization: World Digital Library, Library of Congress

flood.name: The Mona Lisa
flood.source: Musee du Louvre — painted by Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1503-1506
flood.credit: Leonardo da Vinci; digital reproduction: C2RMF (Centre de recherche et de restauration des musees de France)

flood.name: The Taj Mahal
flood.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — mausoleum completed c. 1648, Agra, India, commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan; photograph taken 1865
flood.credit: Photograph, 1865; J. Paul Getty Museum, Open Content Program

flood.name: Girl with a Pearl Earring
flood.source: Mauritshuis, The Hague — painted by Johannes Vermeer, c. 1665
flood.credit: Johannes Vermeer; image: Mauritshuis

flood.name: Newton's Principia (annotated first edition)
flood.source: Wren Library, Trinity College, Cambridge / Cambridge Digital Library — Isaac Newton's own copy of the first edition of Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, published 1687, with his handwritten corrections for the second edition
flood.credit: Photograph: Andrew Dunn (andrewdunnphoto.com); book: Wren Library, Trinity College, Cambridge

flood.name: "The Cow-Pock" - Gillray's Satire on Vaccination
flood.source: Library of Congress (LCCN 94509853) — hand-colored etching by James Gillray, published 1802, satirizing Edward Jenner's smallpox-vaccination practice (Jenner's first vaccination was performed in 1796; the print itself dates to 1802)
flood.credit: James Gillray; Library of Congress

flood.name: The First Photograph
flood.source: Harry Ransom Center, University of Texas at Austin — Niepce's 'View from the Window at Le Gras', created 1826/1827, the oldest surviving camera photograph; image shown is the widely reproduced 1952 high-contrast enhancement by Helmut Gernsheim, since the original bitumen plate is famously faint
flood.credit: Nicephore Niepce (creator); enhanced reproduction by Helmut Gernsheim, ca. 1952, via University of Minnesota / Harry Ransom Center

flood.name: Stephenson's Rocket
flood.source: Science Museum Group — Robert Stephenson and Company's Rocket, built 1829 and winner of the Rainhill Trials that established the steam locomotive standard for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway; image is a period-style 1877/78 engraving, not a modern museum photo of the preserved original (which Commons hosts only under non-free CC BY-SA licences)
flood.credit: Unknown engraver; Popular Science Monthly, vol. 12 (1877-78), via Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
flood.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art (accession/catalog entry 45434) — woodblock print by Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1830-1832, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. NOTE: dated honestly at 1831, outside this era's 1400-1800 window per design-doc instruction; belongs one era later.
flood.credit: Katsushika Hokusai; Metropolitan Museum of Art

flood.name: The Telegraph
flood.source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History — Samuel Morse's electromagnetic telegraph, built with Alfred Vail and first demonstrated 1837/1838; image is an 1872/73 engraving of the Morse instrument
flood.credit: Unknown engraver; Popular Science Monthly, vol. 3 (1872-73), via Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Penny Black
flood.source: British Postal Museum / Royal Mail archives — issued 1 May 1840, the world's first prepaid adhesive postage stamp
flood.credit: William Wyon (Royal Mint engraver, design); Metropolitan Museum of Art, via Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Telephone
flood.source: US Patent Office — Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent US174,465, filed and granted 7 March 1876; priority is genuinely contested, since Elisha Gray filed a competing patent caveat for a similar device on the very same day; image is an 1877/78 engraving of Bell's telephone receiver
flood.credit: Unknown engraver; Popular Science Monthly, vol. 12 (1877-78), via Wikimedia Commons

flood.name: The Brooklyn Bridge
flood.source: National Park Service / Historic American Engineering Record — Brooklyn Bridge, opened 24 May 1883, the longest suspension bridge in the world at the time; image is a period photograph from 1885
flood.credit: Unknown photographer; Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division

flood.name: The Eiffel Tower
flood.source: Exposition Universelle official records — completed 31 March 1889 as the centerpiece of the 1889 Paris World's Fair, engineered by Gustave Eiffel's firm; image is a photochrom print from the Library of Congress, ca. 1890-1905
flood.credit: Unknown photographer; Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division

flood.name: Radio
flood.source: Guglielmo Marconi with the spark-gap transmitter and coherer receiver used in his early long-distance radiotelegraphy experiments, 1901 (LIFE Photo Archive)
flood.credit: LIFE Photo Archive (published anonymously in the UK; PD-anon-70-EU / PD-US)

flood.name: Wright Flyer
flood.source: First flight of the Wright Flyer, Kill Devil Hills, NC, 10:35am, 17 December 1903 (Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Division, digital ID ppprs.00626)
flood.credit: John T. Daniels / Library of Congress

flood.name: Model T
flood.source: 1923 Ford Model T Roadster, Library of Congress collection "Prosperity and Thrift: The Coolidge Era and the Consumer Economy, 1922-1929"
flood.credit: Library of Congress (photographer not credited; PD-US expired)

flood.name: Trinity Test
flood.source: Trinity Site explosion, 0.016 seconds after detonation, 16 July 1945 (Los Alamos National Laboratory photo PA-98-0520)
flood.credit: Berlyn Brixner / Los Alamos National Laboratory

flood.name: ENIAC
flood.source: Glen Beck and Betty Snyder program the ENIAC in building 328 at the Ballistic Research Laboratory, Philadelphia, circa 1947 (U.S. Army photo, ftp.arl.mil historic-computers archive)
flood.credit: U.S. Army (photographer unknown)

flood.name: Sputnik
flood.source: Replica of Sputnik 1 (launched 4 October 1957), National Air and Space Museum; NASA/NSSDC Master Catalog record 1957-001B
flood.credit: NSSDC, NASA

flood.name: Apollo 11
flood.source: Buzz Aldrin's bootprint, lunar surface, 20-21 July 1969 (NASA Photo ID AS11-40-5877)
flood.credit: NASA / Buzz Aldrin
